extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, study section chairs, and grant applicants seeking to understand NIH peer review policies
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of official NIH policies, procedures, and guidance documents governing the conduct, confidentiality, conflict-of-interest handling, and substance of peer review for NIH grant applications (including special instructions for human/animal subjects and award-specific review guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Guidelines for Study Section Reviewers and Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: General Guidelines for Study Section Reviewers and Chairs (guidance document for reviewers and chairs on how to conduct peer review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview of reviewer/chair responsibilities, expected conduct in study sections, and procedural guidance. See linked document for detailed expectations and examples for leading and participating in review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — R Awards (Research Projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for R awards (research projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains evaluation guidance tailored to R-type research project applications (likely addressing significance, investigators, innovation, approach, and environment as applied to research projects). See linked guideline for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — Small Business R Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for Small Business R awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation expectations and criteria specific to small business research awards; consult the linked guidance for scoring nuances and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — F Awards (Fellowship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for fellowship (F) awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on assessing fellowship applications, including trainee candidacy, training environment, and career development plans. See the F Awards guidance document for detailed review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — K Awards (Career Development)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for K (career development) awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criteria focus on career development plan, mentor qualifications, institutional commitment, and research plan suitability. Refer to the K Awards guidance document for detailed scoring and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — P Awards (Program Projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for P (program project/center) awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses evaluation of multi-project, multi-investigator program grants; includes criteria for overall program cohesion, leadership, and individual project merit. See linked P Awards guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — S10 Awards (Shared Instrumentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for S10 shared instrumentation awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on institutional need, access plan, and justification for shared instrumentation. See the S10 guidance document for scoring particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for Reviewers — T Awards (Training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-specific reviewer guidance for T (training) awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include program quality, trainee recruitment and career outcomes, training faculty, and institutional support. Consult the T Awards guidance for full reviewer instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict Of Interest, Confidentiality And Non Disclosure Rules For NIH Peer Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and requirements governing conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and non-disclosure for NIH peer reviewers of grant applications and R&D contract proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what constitutes a conflict, prohibited actions, confidentiality obligations, and reporting requirements. The page links to PDF/MS Word versions of the full policy. Reviewers must follow these rules when handling applications and participating in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Pre-Review Certification Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-review certification form that reviewers must complete prior to participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to certify compliance (e.g., COI/confidentiality) before engaging in review. Linked form provides the exact statements reviewers must acknowledge and sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Post-Review Certification Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review certification form for reviewers to complete after participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to certify actions taken during review and continued compliance. See linked form for required attestations and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects in Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific instructions for reviewers on how to evaluate human subjects protections and related issues in grant and cooperative agreement applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers to assess human subjects protection, inclusion (gender, minorities, children), informed consent, risk/benefit, and data safety monitoring. The linked PDF contains detailed checklists and evaluation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important Notice to Applicants: Requirements for Human and Animal Subjects Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice to applicants detailing requirements related to human and animal subjects in NIH-funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies applicant responsibilities and documentation needed for human/animal subjects sections of applications; reviewers use these requirements when judging compliance. See the linked notice for exact requirements and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-tree tools to guide reviewers on how to handle human subject protection and inclusion questions during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides stepwise procedures for identifying and resolving concerns about protections or inclusion; helps determine whether applications meet NIH policies or require additional action. See linked materials for flowcharts and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Humans / Women / Minorities / Children in Clinical Research Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of documents addressing protection and inclusion of humans, women, minorities, and children in NIH-defined clinical research and Phase III trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes separate guidance/powerpoints for topics: Protection of Humans, Women in Clinical Research, Women in NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trials, Minorities in Clinical Research, Minorities in Phase III Trials, and Children in Human Subjects Research. These set evaluative expectations for inclusion plans and protections; reviewers should consult the relevant document when assessing inclusion and subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on expectations for data and safety monitoring plans (DSMPs) in clinical trials included in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers to evaluate adequacy of monitoring plans, safety oversight, data integrity measures, and whether a DSMB is appropriate. The linked PDF/PPT contains specifics and examples for reviewer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Regulations (42 CFR Part 52h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulations (42 CFR Part 52h) governing the scientific peer review of research grant applications and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/regulatory standards that define procedural requirements for peer review, confidentiality, and handling of conflicts and appeals; includes Final Rules and Federal Register notice. Reviewers and administrators must follow these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Best Practice Guidelines for Accepting Additional Grant Application Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice guidance describing when and how NIH will accept additional materials submitted with grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains acceptable scenarios, documentation, timing, and handling procedures for supplementary materials. Reviewers may receive additional materials per these procedures; see the linked document for detailed policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Policy on Submission of Additional Grant Application Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy statement on submission of additional application materials to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal policy (distinct from best-practice guidance) for accepting additional materials, including procedures and limitations. Reviewers should apply this policy when considering whether materials are allowable and how they affect review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Submission Policy and Eligibility Lists (NOT-OD Notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and notices (e.g., NOT-OD-09-155, NOT-OD-09-114, NOT-OD-08-026) describing modified application submission, referral and review procedures for reviewers with recent substantial service and for appointed members; includes lists of reviewers eligible for continuous submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines eligibility criteria for continuous submission, how recent service affects submission/referral/review, and which reviewers are exempt/affected. Linked PDFs list eligible individuals and explain frequency and process implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Initial Scientific Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and criteria for appealing the outcome of an initial scientific peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes grounds for appeal, required documentation, timelines, and how appeals are handled administratively. Reviewers and applicants should consult the appeals guidance to understand procedural remedies and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Implements New Procedures to Protect NIH Application Data Sent to Peer Reviewers on Compact Disks
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to protect application data when distributing materials (specifically mentions compact disks) to peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies data protection measures and handling procedures to maintain confidentiality and security of application materials during distribution and review. See the linked notice for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Notes / Peer Review Archive / OER Peer Review Policy Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections and archives of peer review policy documents, news, and updates maintained by OER/CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve as sources for historical policy changes, notices, and guidance. Reviewers and administrators should consult these archives for context and past policy language; individual entries contain the operative rubrics and procedures.
